elements.description: An agent's request for approval, with Approve / Deny, an optional countdown, and a compact row once decided.

properties.name: heading
properties.description: The action, e.g. "Send campaign email" – the group's name

properties.name: description
properties.description: One line of context below the heading: text, or an element (cloned)

properties.name: risk
properties.description: Tinted badge in the header; leave out to hide it

properties.name: icon
properties.description: Icon element in the header tile (cloned) – defaults to a small shield

properties.name: details
properties.description: Key-value rows in the preview, e.g. To, Subject, Scheduled

properties.name: preview
properties.description: Anything to show above the details, e.g. a recipient list: text, or an element (cloned)

properties.name: status
properties.description: The status

properties.name: onApprove
properties.description:
Called on Approve with the "Always allow" choice. Return a promise to show a spinner and lock the card until it
settles; a rejection keeps it pending and shows `errorLabel`, and Approve can be pressed again to retry

properties.name: errorLabel
properties.description: Shown under the buttons when an onApprove promise rejects

properties.name: editable
properties.description: Shows an "Edit" button (it fires tc-edit)

properties.name: expiresIn
properties.description: Seconds until the request expires and is denied with reason "timeout"

properties.name: allowStopTimer
properties.description: Show a "Stop" button next to the countdown that turns the time limit off (WCAG 2.2.1). Default true

properties.name: stopTimerLabel
properties.description: Its label – the countdown ("Expires in 42 seconds…") describes it

properties.name: allowAlways
properties.description: Show the "Always allow this action" checkbox. Default true

properties.name: alwaysLabel
properties.description: The "Always allow" checkbox's label

properties.name: approveLabel
properties.description: The Approve button's label

properties.name: denyLabel
properties.description: The Deny button's label

properties.name: editLabel
properties.description: The Edit button's label (shown with `editable`)

properties.name: shortcuts
properties.description: Show ⌘↵ / Esc hints on the buttons (the shortcuts work either way). Default true

properties.name: label
properties.description: Small label on the gray tray above the card, e.g. "Step 4 · gmail.send": text, or an element (cloned)

properties.name: actions
properties.description: Where the buttons sit: on the gray tray below the card or inside the white card. Default: "tray" in the Standard look, "card" in the Clean look

properties.name: why
properties.description: "Why you're seeing this": one line on what made the agent ask, e.g. the rule or threshold it met

properties.name: whyLabel
properties.description: The heading of the `why` line

properties.name: consequences
properties.description: What happens if the person approves, and if they deny – one sentence each

properties.name: ifApproveLabel
properties.description: The heading of the approve consequence

properties.name: ifDenyLabel
properties.description: The heading of the deny consequence

properties.name: editableDetails
properties.description: Shows "Edit arguments", which turns the text details into fields; each change fires tc-details-change

properties.name: editDetailsLabel
properties.description: The "Edit arguments" button's label

properties.name: doneDetailsLabel
properties.description: The button's label while editing

properties.name: evidence
properties.description: Sources the request rests on, shown as chips

properties.name: evidenceLabel
properties.description: The heading of the evidence chips

properties.name: look
properties.description: Visual style: "standard" or "clean"; unset follows <tc-look-provider>, else "standard"

events.name: tc-status-change
events.description: The card was approved, denied or expired; detail `{ status }`. Cancelable: preventDefault() keeps the status (controlled use)

events.name: tc-deny
events.description: Denied by the user or by the countdown; detail `{ reason: "user" | "timeout" }`

events.name: tc-expire
events.description: The countdown ran out (tc-deny fires too)

events.name: tc-details-change
events.description: An argument was edited in "Edit arguments" mode; detail `{ details, index, label, value }`. Cancelable: preventDefault() keeps the rows (controlled use)

events.name: tc-evidence-select
events.description: An evidence chip without `href` was pressed; detail `{ evidence, index }`

props.name: description
props.description: One line of context below the title

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon in the header tile – defaults to a small shield

props.name: details
props.description: Key-value rows in the preview, e.g. To, Subject, Scheduled

props.name: preview
props.description: Anything to show above the details, e.g. a recipient list – children work too

props.name: label
props.description: Small label on the gray tray above the card

props.name: status
props.description: The status. Controlled when defined – the card then only asks for changes through `onStatusChange`

props.name: onStatusChange
props.description: Called with the new status whenever the card is approved, denied or expires (controlled or not)

props.name: onDeny
props.description: Called when the card is denied, by the user or by the countdown (`reason: "timeout"`)

props.name: onExpire
props.description: Called when the countdown runs out (onDeny is called too)

props.name: onDetailsChange
props.type: (details: ApprovalDetail[], change: { index: number; label: string; value: string }) => void
props.description:
With `editableDetails`, called with the rows after an argument is edited. Given, the rows are controlled – pass
them back as `details`; without it the card keeps the edits itself

props.name: onEvidenceSelect
props.description: Called when an evidence chip without `href` is pressed

changelog: `tc-approval-card` gains decision detail: why you're seeing it, what each choice does, editable arguments and evidence chips.

features.name: light-dark()
features.why: Every colour token is a light / dark pair; without it no colour token resolves.

features.name: color-mix()
features.why: Tints and washes mixed from the tokens.

features.name: Container size queries
features.why: Components adapt to the width they're given, not the window's.

features.name: inert
features.why: Closed and leaving parts are out of the tab order and hidden from screen readers.

features.name: :is() and :where()
features.why: Every rule is keyed on :where() so the page can override it.

features.name: adoptedStyleSheets
features.without: Each element type's CSS goes into one <style> element in <head> instead – it looks and works the same.

features.name: forced-colors media query
features.without: In a forced-colours mode the browser's own adjustments apply, without the components' fixes.
